question: Which of the following can produce a virtual image larger than the object?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A concave mirror can produce a virtual image larger than the object when the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror.
 
• The virtual image formed by a concave mirror is upright and magnified compared to the object.
 
• In a concave mirror, the magnification increases as the object moves closer to the mirror within the focal point range.
 
• This property of concave mirrors is utilized in devices such as makeup mirrors and shaving mirrors, where a larger, upright image is desirable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a type of spherical mirror where the reflective surface bulges inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• It converges light rays that are parallel to its principal axis, focusing them at a point known as the focal point.
 
• Depending on the object's position relative to the focal point, concave mirrors can produce both real and virtual images.
 
• Applications include telescopes, headlights, and reflecting telescopes.
 
 
 
• **Plane Mirror:**
 
 
• A plane mirror has a flat reflective surface.
 
• It always produces a virtual image that is the same size as the object and is upright and laterally inverted (left-right inverted).
 
• Plane mirrors are commonly used in everyday life, such as in bathrooms and dressing rooms.
 
 
 
• **Concave Lens:**
 
 
• A concave lens is a lens that is thinner at the center than at the edges.
 
• It diverges light rays that pass through it, spreading them outwards.
 
• Concave lenses always produce virtual, upright, and reduced images.
 
• They are used in devices like eyeglasses for nearsightedness and in some optical instruments.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror:**
 
 
• A convex mirror has a reflective surface that bulges outward.
 
• It diverges light rays, spreading them outward.
 
• Convex mirrors always produce virtual, upright, and reduced images.
 
• Common applications include vehicle side mirrors and security mirrors.
